key_insight: Crosswind kite wakes have a modest effect on lift, but modeling rotor-slipstream deflection near the wing can reverse the predicted rotor effect.
engineering_relevance: Wake-aware modeling supports airborne wind energy performance estimates and farm spacing decisions, including downstream aerodynamic power losses.
method: Vortex step aerodynamics coupled to a time-marching free vortex wake in OpenFAWE.
Lumped-mass tether and actuator-disc rotors represented by shed vortex rings.
Fixed-kite, crosswind-loop and two-kite simulations with wake-resolution checks.
evidence_signal: Validation showed lift agreement within 0.3% of an independent vortex step code and 3.1% of RANS for the inflatable kite; simulations predicted a 2.2% downstream aerodynamic power loss at one loop diameter.
watch_item: Free rotor rings did not converge with time-step refinement, and slipstream treatment changed the predicted lift effect from +1.9% to −3.5%.
paper_title: Free-vortex-wake dynamics of airborne wind energy kites in crosswind flight
